New coverage at this checkpoint:
- ByteBarn: host-bound compressed XOR codec, hidden child stdin routing, command-message fields, HTTP options and host registration; archive correlation to a C# script execution host and startup activation. The executable was inspected through static .NET metadata, not executed.
- XAMPP manager: WhatsApp QR callback data reaches a remote image URL; message body supplies an unquoted shell argument. Local QR rendering, public QR data and execFile argument arrays are negative controls.
- Filename shell breakout: match complete source string nodes, avoiding escaped fragments from ordinary quoted command paths.

Neutral taxonomy repairs preserve observations while removing unsupported intent: session-store/deletion cooccurrence, OS-identity/HTTP context, long-duration activation context, task/state-gate context, short token-to-hex maps, decoded Buffer evaluation syntax, reversed URL encodings, administrative WhatsApp vocabulary, and media filename/text type disagreement. See v6-migrations.json in the report directory for old/new IDs.

Marketplace comparisons are member-by-member, not publisher-name allowlisting. Quokka, Claude history viewer, Qodana, Wallaby Python, Code Runner, Atlas HCL and Atlascode matched published member content. Snyk preview variants differ only in package.json whitespace; parsed manifests are identical. Comparison evidence is under /var/tmp/vsix-triage/official-comparisons.

All sample handling was static. No extension was installed or activated, and no sample JavaScript or executable was run.

The v7 prompt regression preserves concealed-action detection while excluding explicit product guidance about base-model branding. Twenty Bandit versions match Marketplace archives byte for byte. A WGSL darwin-arm64 comparison required the targetPlatform query; the matching build is byte-identical. The first default-platform comparison selected alpine-x64 and was not equivalent.
